title: Minimize prefill latency using async host-to-GPU copy scheduler and lightweight threadpool
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Host-side overhead during large prefill/encode batches is a consistent contributor to tail latency. We observe: (1) synchronous host->GPU memcpy and blocking kernel submission in the prefill path, (2) a large, shared threadpool with contention between IO copy tasks and higher-priority runtime orchestration tasks, and (3) suboptimal decision logic for zero-copy vs pinned-copy that causes unnecessary CPU work on small/bursty requests. Goal: Reduce end-to-end prefill latency and tail variance by introducing an asynchronous copy scheduler, reducing memory copy counts via pinning/zero-copy heuristics, and slimming the threadpool contention surface so orchestration threads are never starved.
acceptance_criteria: P50 prefill latency reduced by >= 20% on the long-sequence benchmark (seq=2048) compared to baseline runtime-1.21
P95 prefill latency reduced by >= 15% and P99 improved measurably under synthetic arrival bursts
No regression in decode latency or token throughput for throughput-heavy workloads (within 5%)
New async copy scheduler is covered by unit tests and integration test harness (CI job) and has flamegraph-based perf regression guard
Benchmarks and perf dashboards (Console) updated with before/after traces and cost impact analysis
comments: 2026-03-05 Maya Patel: Created ticket after spike showing ~35ms avg host copy + queueing overhead for 2k-token prefill on T4-like instances. Collected eBPF traces and per-thread timelines. Draft design sketched: dedicated IO worker per GPU that accepts zero-copy/pinned-copy tasks, per-stream CUDA events for overlap, and a small submission queue to avoid blocking the runtime main loop.

2026-03-07 Diego Ramos: Spike implementation shows 18% P50 improvement when using page-locked buffers and overlapped memcpy with kernel launches on a local test rig. Observed threadpool contention still visible for high concurrency; need to isolate orchestration workers.

2026-03-09 Review (Ben Cho - infra): Recommended replacing a shared std::deque with a lock-free MPSC queue for the IO worker to reduce contention. Also suggested a heuristic: for batches < 8 sequences prefer zero-copy path; for > 8 use pinned-copy to amortize pin cost.

2026-03-10 Diego Ramos: Implemented MPSC queue and per-GPU IO threads; added adaptive threshold for zero-copy vs pinned-copy. Running CI perf job overnight. Kept a fallback synchronous path for older kernels/drivers.

2026-03-11 QA (Ayesha Khan): Integration smoke passed on small clusters, but observed one regression: model compile stage occasionally blocks when IO thread spikes. Added task profiling and limited IO concurrency to 2 simultaneous DMA-style operations to stabilize.
2026-03-11 Maya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require no more than 5% throughput regression. Filing follow-up ENG subtask for kernel-selection non-blocking path (ENG-12016).
